text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Blood pressure plan agreed with him: home readings twice a day, sodium under 1500 to 2300 mg a day, potassium-rich fruit and vegetables, his daily walk, and amlodipine started at 2.5 mg; a thiazide is avoided for now because of his low weight, fasting, and the risk of low sodium and potassium
  • Clinical nutrition consultation with a registered dietitian: nutrition-focused assessment, energy and protein targets within his lacto-vegetarian diet, vitamin B12, vitamin D, and calcium, and a plan for the fast and for refeeding
  • Fast safety plan, respecting his decision: water with a pinch of salt and some citrus juice as he chooses, about 2 L a day; home blood pressure lying and standing twice a day; amlodipine held on fast days; rise slowly; a daily telephone check; call or come in for fainting, chest pain, palpitations, confusion, or vomiting
  • High-risk refeeding protocol (NICE CG32): thiamine 300 mg a day from before the first meal for 10 days; start at about 10 kcal/kg a day and reach full needs over 4 to 7 days; prophylactic potassium, phosphate, and magnesium; electrolytes before feeding and daily for the first 3 days, then until stable
  • Vitamin B12 1 mg and vitamin D 1000 units by mouth daily, with recheck of B12, methylmalonic acid, blood count, and vitamin D after three to four months
  • Bone health: DXA and FRAX; about 1000 to 1200 mg of calcium a day from milk and curd; weight-bearing and balance exercise; no osteoporosis drug while FRAX is below treatment thresholds; repeat DXA in two years
  • Falls and orthostatic checks: lying and standing blood pressure at every visit, extra fluids in hot weather, and a yearly Timed Up and Go
  • CMID hypertension monitoring: blood pressure and weight every visit; a metabolic panel, lipids, urine albumin, and HbA1c yearly; baseline ECG and echocardiogram for stage 2; a yearly eye examination, depression screen, and cardiovascular risk estimate

resource.title: Mahatma Gandhi synthetic care plan
resource.description: Treat stage 2 hypertension in a thin, lacto-vegetarian 70-year-old man by the 1939 AHA/ACC guideline and the CMID schedule, choosing a drug and hold rules that suit a man who fasts; assess nutrition, protein, vitamin B12, vitamin D, and bone health within his diet; and, through shared decision-making that respects his fasting as an act of conscience, plan a seven-day fast and a NICE CG32 high-risk refeeding protocol (thiamine first, slow energy increase, prophylactic potassium, phosphate, and magnesium, and early electrolyte checks), with orthostatic checks and falls prevention throughout.
